_note: Built by /crew:verify on 2026-09-13 against 5238be3d. Every `run` command
below was TIMED on this machine before it was written down; the seconds in
each `why` are measurements, not estimates. This file is TRACKED as of 2026-09-14:
.gitignore un-ignores !.crew/verify.json, so this file DOES travel;
CI (push only on main, plus pull_request, workflow_dispatch and a nightly schedule where a matrix runs; PR runs 3.12 only, superseded PR runs cancelled, main never cancelled - see #279) is the
gate that everyone else gets; this map only makes the LOCAL Stop gate
selective. Do not read it as the whole of this repo's verification.
`unmapped` is `fail`, but be precise about what that buys: the first rule
claims `plugin/**` and `skills/**` so that EVERY content change reaches the
version-bump check, and that makes it a catch-all. A brand-new test file
under plugin/crew/tests/ therefore matches, and `unmapped` does NOT fire on
it. So this file does not enforce crew-verification's authoring contract -
a check added without its rule is silently not run, and the only thing that
reconciles that is skills/crew-setup/scripts/map-audit.sh. Measured: 0 of
790 tracked files are unmapped, which is a fact about coverage, not proof
that a new check would be noticed.
`default` is NOT a general floor, and should not be read as one. verify-gate
falls back to it only when the matched rules contributed NO commands at all
(verify-gate.sh:247), so with rules this broad the only way to reach it is a
turn that changes nothing but files inside the two `run: []` rules - in
practice a graphify-out-only or workflow-only turn. It is kept because those
are real turns and 7s of smoke is a better answer there than nothing.
There is deliberately no `always` key: any entry in it would make `cmds`
non-empty every time and `default` unreachable.
`seconds` is the rule's MEASURED cost, and it is the field verify-gate
reads for the Stop budget (verify.stopBudgetSeconds, default 60). It
replaces nothing: `why` keeps the reason, `seconds` carries the number,
because the costs used to live only as prose inside `why` ("8s", "29s",
"245s") and nothing could parse them. A rule with NO `seconds` is UNKNOWN
cost, which is NOT free: it always runs and the gate says its cost is
unstated. Most rules here are deliberately in that state - only the ones
actually timed carry a number, and filling the rest in by guesswork would
be exactly the fiction the field exists to replace. Re-time rather than
trusting these: measured on a quiet tree 2026-09-18/19. The whole-suite rule
(rules[8], `python3 -m pytest plugin/crew/tests/ -q`) was re-priced 2026-09-24
from the then-current 185 (itself the midpoint of five runs spanning 157-201s,
which were partial or otherwise not the full serial suite) to a measured
full-serial 1928s, and re-priced again the same day (crew 1.0 F4) to 377s -
measured on THIS host (Linux, 20 CPUs, lightly loaded - see that rule's own
`why` for the full host/load/process record the 1928s figure omitted, which
is why it was superseded rather than reconciled: an unannotated number
cannot be re-derived or compared against a load figure that does not exist).
The two are not a claimed speedup of the same work - see the rule's own `why`.
non-empty every time and `default` unreachable.

Each changed file in the review bundle is linted at its base blob and at its bundle blob; a finding the bundle ADDS
(keyed path+rule+message, line numbers ignored) refuses the round with exit 9. A tool that is missing, crashes, times
out, prints unparseable output or cannot parse a changed file is COULD NOT CHECK - never a pass - and also refuses
unless --allow-unverified. check-marketplace.py, self-claims and version drift are NOT here: the verify gate already
runs them (rules[0] and the docs/scripts rules) and the review preflight already refuses a tree that gate has not passed.

repo-wide at ffd11270 - they block only when a bundle adds one). shellcheck/actionlint: not on PATH on the Linux host,
so they run through pinned uvx packages. psscriptanalyzer: an allowlist of correctness and fail-open rules measured
against the 466 findings over the 44 tracked PowerShell files at ffd11270 (230 PSAvoidUsingWriteHost and the other
style rules - nouns, verbs, ShouldProcess, positional parameters - are deliberately not listed).
